cohort: 300 pregnant women (150 normotensive and 150 prehypertensive based on third-trimester blood pressure) delivering at Jinja Regional Referral Hospital in Uganda, whose neonates were followed until death or hospital discharge.
finding: Late pregnancy prehypertension significantly increased the risk for composite adverse neonatal outcomes, specifically Small-for-Gestation Age (SGA) and stillbirth, and was associated with a decrease in birthweight.
followup_time: Until hospital discharge or death of the neonate
